stem: The theory that states “pieces of the earth’s crust are in constant, slow motion driven by movement in the mantle” is called
expl: The theory states that pieces (plates) of the Earth’s crust keep moving slowly due to mantle motion is the Plate Tectonics Theory. According to this theory, the Earth’s crust is divided into many small and large plates. These tectonic plates move independently in different directions over the asthenosphere. The various landforms produced due to these plate movements are studied under plate tectonics.

stem: The theory of continental drift was developed by?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: The Continental Drift Theory was developed by Alfred Wegener. According to Wegener, the splitting of Pangaea began about 200 million years ago. Pangaea first split into two large continental blocks—Laurasia and Gondwanaland—as the northern and southern landmasses, respectively. Later, Laurasia and Gondwanaland gradually broke into many smaller parts, which form today’s continents.

stem: Continents have drifted apart because of-
expl: Plate tectonic activity is considered the most appropriate reason for the separation of continents. The upper part of the Earth (the entire crust and the upper mantle) is made up of different plates. These plates become mobile in various patterns due to tectonic processes. Thus, these plates shift the continents and oceanic regions lying on them along with their own movement.

Orogenic forces are intense horizontal endogenic forces that cause extreme folding, faulting and deformation of the earth's crust resulting in mountain building. Under this, two types of forces work—compressional force and tensional force. Due to compressional force, rock layers bend, which is called “folding”. The upfolded part is called “anticline”, and the downfolded part is called “syncline”.

stem: regarding a sedimentary rocks which of the following statements is true?

options.label: a
options.text: These are such rocks whose structure depends on temperature and pressure

options.label: c
options.text: These rocks are deposited in layers

options.label: d
options.text: These rocks cannot be formed in water

expl: Layered or sedimentary rocks are formed when debris obtained from the breaking and weathering of rocks keeps getting deposited in water. Sedimentary rocks are formed not only in water but also by other agents of erosion such as wind, glaciers, etc. They contain adequate amounts of remains of organisms and plant fragments. Sedimentary rocks spread on the Earth’s surface are layered, i.e., they are deposited in strata.

stem: Which one of the following rocks is not a metamorphic rock?
expl: Among the given options, dolomite is a sedimentary rock. Gneiss is formed by metamorphism of granite, and quartzite is formed by metamorphism of quartz-rich sandstone.

expl: Igneous rocks are formed when magma (inside the Earth) and lava (on the outer surface) cool and solidify. They do not have layers and fossils are also not found in them. They are both crystalline and non-crystalline.

stem: Minerals are deposited and accumulated in the strata of which of the following rocks?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Minerals are deposited in sedimentary rocks (layered rocks). Sedimentary rocks are formed when the debris obtained from the breaking and weathering of rocks remains deposited in water. Remains of organisms and plants are found in them in very small quantities. By the metamorphism of sedimentary rocks, rocks such as slate, marble, gneiss, etc. are formed.
